title: Rate, gradient and accumulated volume
subject: Mathematics
related_theory: Q(t)=b+mt; dQ/dt=m; V(t)−V(0)=bt+mt²/2. Use the signed difference of the antiderivative at the two cursors. Initial inventory zero for the default example.
practical: Flow logging or weighed accumulation; EXP01 optional
design_task: Determine b for a target volume given m and endpoints; zero duration makes the inverse unidentifiable. Challenge: equal final flows can have different inventories.
learning_outcome: At what instant is a vessel filling fastest? Move a tangent and two time cursors on the same trace. Students often read the height of a flow trace as its accumulated volume.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Continuity through a contraction
subject: Fluids
related_theory: A=πD²/4; v=Q/A; ṁ=ρQ. Two stations share Q by steady incompressible continuity. Positive axial direction downstream. Density fixed at 1000 kg/m³.
practical: EXP01 measured flow and line geometry
design_task: Choose a bore to meet a velocity ceiling at fixed delivery; report feasible available bores. Explain why shrinking a real nozzle on a fixed pump may change Q.
learning_outcome: Pinch a pipe while holding throughput fixed. Predict which cross-section has greater mean velocity and whether mass flow changes.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Hydrostatic pressure and datum
subject: Fluids
related_theory: dp/dz=−ρg with z upward; p_abs=p_surface+ρgh for depth h down from the free surface. g=9.80665 m/s²; local atmosphere for gauge display fixed at 101325 Pa.
practical: Static water-column pressure check; EXP01 tap-datum preparation
design_task: Infer depth from gauge reading allowing nonatmospheric surface pressure; unknown surface pressure makes the inverse nonunique.
learning_outcome: Lower a pressure tap and switch the display between absolute and gauge pressure. A wider vessel feels intuitively heavier but does not change the pressure at a fixed depth.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Bernoulli and the mechanical energy balance
subject: Fluids
related_theory: p₂=p₁+ρg[z₁−z₂+hₚ−hL]+ρ(v₁²−v₂²)/2; vᵢ=4Q/(πDᵢ²); hL=K v₂²/(2g). z₁=0; ρ=1000 kg/m³; g=9.80665 m/s². K referenced to station 2; kinetic energy factors both one.
practical: EXP01 single pump and EXP02 system curve
design_task: Choose pump head to recover a required outlet pressure; explain the difference between pressure recovery and energy dissipation. Introduce measured losses for a real rig.
learning_outcome: Given a narrowing pipe that rises, predict the downstream tap reading. Toggle losses to discover which head is dissipated and which terms can be recovered.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Laminar pipe velocity and shear
subject: Fluids
related_theory: u(r)=2v̄[1−(r/R)²]; v̄=Q/(πR²); Δp/L=8μv̄/R²; τrz=μ du/dr=−4μv̄r/R²; Re=2ρRv̄/μ. ρ=1000 kg/m³.
practical: Separate laminar capillary demonstration; EXP02 only if regime and taps qualify
design_task: Find Q for a wall shear limit; determine whether the answer is laminar. Transfer to a viscous liquid at fixed Q and explain which field changes.
learning_outcome: Drag a radial probe through the flow and reconstruct the mean from annular areas. Centreline velocity and cross-sectional mean are commonly confused.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Flat-plate momentum and thermal boundary layers
subject: Fluids
related_theory: η=y√(U/(νx)); f‴+½ f f″=0, f(0)=f′(0)=0, f′(∞)=1; u/U=f′; Reₓ=Ux/ν; δ₉₉≈4.91√(νx/U); τw=.33206ρU²/√Reₓ; Cf,x=.6641/√Reₓ, mean Cf=1.3282/√ReL. ReL=UL/ν uses plate length, not an average Reynolds number.
practical: Independent flat-plate teaching data; no claimed FlexBench capability
design_task: Choose x for a target layer thickness and test sensitivity to U. Higher fidelity requires pressure gradient, disturbance and transition data; turbulent comparison can use a separately reviewed correlation. Distinguish δ₉₉ from displacement thickness.
learning_outcome: Move a probe downstream and explain why the layer thickens while local wall shear decreases. Compare local quantities with length averages on the same plate.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Reynolds number and competing scales
subject: Fluids
related_theory: Re=ρvD/μ=vD/ν; constant-Q mode derives v=4Q/(πD²). Default prescribed-speed mode. For external flow replace D with distance from the leading edge and use free-stream U.
practical: EXP01/02 pipe geometry, flow and viscosity
design_task: Choose D for a target Re under each constraint. Transfer to a stirred tank and identify the new characteristic velocity/length before using any correlation.
learning_outcome: Hold velocity constant and double diameter, then repeat holding Q constant. Predict the opposite changes in Re and identify the variable the equipment actually holds.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Darcy friction and pressure loss
subject: Fluids
related_theory: v=4Q/(πD²); Δp=fD (L/D)ρv²/2 where fD is the Darcy factor; laminar fD=64/Re; turbulent 1/√fD=−2log₁₀[ε/(3.7D)+2.51/(Re√fD)]. ρ=1000 kg/m³, μ=.001 Pa·s.
practical: EXP02 only with suitable straight-pipe differential taps
design_task: Solve required head for each available bore; compare fixed-f assumption and roughness sensitivity. Use bisection on s=1/√f over [1,30], residual <10⁻¹⁰.
learning_outcome: Trace a pipe operating point onto the Moody axes; roughness changes can matter very differently at two flow rates.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Pump and system operating point
subject: Fluids
related_theory: Hₚ=s²H₀−aQ²; Hs=Hz+bQ²; Q*=√[(s²H₀−Hz)/(a+b)] when numerator positive. Shaft power=ρgQH/η only with specified efficiency. Synthetic centrifugal curve; Q in m³/s. g=9.80665, ρ=1000.
practical: EXP01 and EXP02; EXP03 extension
design_task: Choose speed and restriction for a required flow, then compare input power; hydraulic throttling trades off against delivered head. Compare EXP01 pump data and EXP02 resistance.
learning_outcome: Throttle a valve and follow the intersection of pump and system curves. Ask whether a speed command fixes the flow.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Pipe selection and pump duty
subject: Equipment design
related_theory: A=πD²/4; v=Q/A; Hreq=Δz+(fL/D+ΣK)v²/(2g); Pshaft=ρgQHreq/η. Use prescribed Darcy f for first release; advanced mode delegates to the friction block. ρ=1000, g=9.80665.
practical: EXP01/02 design tutorial
design_task: Filter v≤vmax; rank by energy and bore, preserve nondominated candidates. For pump selection use S09 teaching curve at a speed that meets Hreq, subject to allowed speed and forward range; missing vendor evidence means preliminary duty only.
learning_outcome: Can two feasible pipe sizes meet the same delivery with different energy use? Compare a catalogue of internal diameters against a defined design basis.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Fourier conduction through a composite wall
subject: Heat transfer
related_theory: R″=L₁/k₁+Rc″+L₂/k₂; q″=(Th−Tc)/R″; Q̇=Aq″; interface faces Th−q″L₁/k₁ and Tc+q″L₂/k₂. Positive heat flux left to right; isothermal external faces; A=1 m².
practical: Proposed instrumented wall specimen; lecture-ready without equipment
design_task: Choose minimum L₂ to meet a heat-flux limit within a depth constraint; flag already feasible and impossible cases. Repeat with a worse contact and explain the interface temperatures.
learning_outcome: Move a material interface and change its conductivity separately. Thickness changes resistance; the intrinsic conductivity of a homogeneous constant-property material stays fixed.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Cylindrical insulation and critical radius
subject: Heat transfer
related_theory: Rcond=ln(ro/ri)/(2πkL); Rconv=1/(2πrohL); Q̇=(Ti−T∞)/(Rcond+Rconv); rc=k/h; T(r)=Ti−Q̇ ln(r/ri)/(2πkL). L=1 m. Fixed inner surface temperature.
practical: Independent insulated-cylinder demonstration
design_task: Bracket on each side of rc, report all thicknesses for a target magnitude; impose any space cap after solving. At zero driving force no unique insulation design.
learning_outcome: Add insulation to a small isothermal cylinder. Predict the sign of the first change in heat loss before seeing the curve.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Transient heating and cooling
subject: Heat transfer
related_theory: Infinite slab of half-thickness L, two identical convecting faces, Lc=V/As=L. Bi=hL/k, α=k/(ρcp), Fo=αt/L²; lumped T=T∞+(Ti−T∞)exp[−h t/(ρcp L)]. For distributed comparator solve ∂T/∂t=αTxx; Tx(0)=0, −kTx(L)=h(Ts−T∞), initial T=Ti. ρcp=2.0×10⁶ J/(m³ K).
practical: Proposed thermal module; instrumented slab for spatial validation
design_task: Solve elapsed time to a target strictly between initial and ambient. Reach equilibrium asymptotically; do not return a finite time at exactly ambient.
learning_outcome: Compare the surface of a thick slab with its centre. A good exponential fit to one sensor does not by itself establish uniform temperature.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Convection from a plate and the Nusselt number
subject: Heat transfer
related_theory: Uniform wall T, laminar plate: Reₓ=Ux/ν; Nuₓ=.332 Reₓ^½ Pr^⅓; NūL=.664 ReL^½ Pr^⅓; hx=Nuₓ kf/x; h̄=NūL kf/L; Q̇=h̄WL(Tw−T∞). W=1 m, x=L for default local result, ν=1.5×10⁻⁵ m²/s, kf=.026 W/(m K). Coefficients approximate similarity solution.
practical: Independent isothermal plate; separate from internal-flow rig
design_task: Choose U to meet a target heat duty under a velocity cap. Compare whole-face and trailing-edge estimates. Transfer to internal flow and identify boundary condition data required before selecting a correlation.
learning_outcome: Move a local heat-flux probe from the leading edge and compare it with a calorimeter measuring the whole plate.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Heat exchanger performance and flow arrangement
subject: Heat transfer
related_theory: Ch=ṁh cp,h; Cc=ṁc cp,c; Cr=Cmin/Cmax; N=UA/Cmin; εparallel=[1−exp(−N(1+Cr))]/(1+Cr); εcounter=[1−exp(−N(1−Cr))]/[1−Cr exp(−N(1−Cr))]. At Cr=1 counter ε=N/(1+N). Q̇=εCmin(Thi−Tci); Tho=Thi−Q̇/Ch, Tco=Tci+Q̇/Cc.
practical: Proposed heat-exchanger module; confirm stream vs bath boundary
design_task: Choose the arrangement for a required duty and explain when terminal outlet temperatures can cross without local reversal. A bucket with a submerged coil is a different bath boundary condition.
learning_outcome: Reverse the cold stream while keeping both inlet conditions fixed. Compare the cold outlet with the hot outlet and the local approach temperature.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Heat exchanger area and feasible duty
subject: Equipment design
related_theory: From target Q̇ calculate terminal temperatures using Ch,Cc. For counterflow ΔT₁=Thi−Tco, ΔT₂=Tho−Tci; for parallel use inlet and outlet differences. ΔTlm=(ΔT₁−ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂), limit ΔT₁=ΔT₂. A=Q̇/(Udirty ΔTlm); 1/Udirty=1/Uclean+Rf″.
practical: Proposed heat-exchanger module, preliminary duty exercise
design_task: Enumerate both layouts, filter area cap, report Pareto between required area and assumed fouling margin; simulate achieved duty after rounding area upward. Utilities require their own flow/temperature basis.
learning_outcome: Move a duty target towards the maximum and observe why area grows rapidly. Diagnose an infeasible request before entering the root solver.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Diffusive flux and transient concentration
subject: Mass transfer
related_theory: Steady J=−D(C₂−C₁)/L. Semi-infinite transient C(x,t)=Ci+(Cs−Ci)erfc[x/(2√(Dt))], C(0,t)=Cs, C(∞,t)=Ci. In transient mode C₁=Cs and C₂=Ci; at t=0 handle surface jump separately.
practical: Independent tracer diffusion or membrane coupon demonstration
design_task: Choose steady barrier thickness to limit flux, then explain why using that relation for breakthrough time is unjustified.
learning_outcome: Distinguish a steady gradient through a membrane from a front entering an initially uniform medium. Doubling thickness and doubling time have different effects.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Dynamic tank mass and level balance
subject: Balances
related_theory: d(Ah)/dt=Qin−Qout. Default pumped outlet at fixed Qout; h=h₀+(Qin−Qout)t/A. Alternative gravity Qout=Cd Ao√(2gh), g=9.80665 m/s², Cd=.62, Ao=.0002 m². Empty/full events at h=0,H=2 m. Stop at first boundary and report remaining requested duration.
practical: Manual tank inventory or proposed level module
design_task: Find capacity required over a pulsed feed sequence; or determine gravity equilibrium (Qin/CdAo)²/(2g) and check vessel limits. Compare level-only vs separate outlet data.
learning_outcome: A tank receives a step in feed flow. Predict whether the level changes instantly and whether a new steady level exists.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: CSTR concentration response
subject: Reaction engineering
related_theory: V dC/dt=Q(Cin−C)−kVC; D=Q/V; C∞=D Cin/(D+k); C(t)=C∞+(C₀−C∞)exp[−(D+k)t]. Fixed volume, equal inlet/outlet. Conservative tracer k=0.
practical: Proposed CSTR with calibrated conductivity tracer
design_task: Estimate k from a trace only after V/Q and sensor dynamics are constrained. Use a benign salt tracer for physical mixing comparison; tracer response alone cannot validate reaction kinetics.
learning_outcome: Change the inlet concentration of a mixed tank, then distinguish hydraulic residence time from the faster concentration response of a reacting system.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: CSTR versus PFR performance and sizing
subject: Reaction engineering
related_theory: For −rA=kCA, constant density: XC=kτ/(1+kτ); XP=1−exp(−kτ); VC=(Q/k)X/(1−X); VP=−(Q/k)ln(1−X). Plot FA0/(−rA)=Q/[k(1−X)] against conversion. τ=V/Q.
practical: Proposed CSTR; PFR comparison is virtual until separately measured
design_task: Given a volume budget choose reactor type or tanks in series; report infeasible targets or multiple viable configurations. Higher-order kinetics requires experimental rates.
learning_outcome: Place a rectangle and the area under a rate curve on a Levenspiel plot. Predict which ideal reactor needs more volume at equal conversion.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Arrhenius temperature sensitivity
subject: Reaction engineering
related_theory: k(T)=kref exp[−Ea/R(1/T−1/Tref)]; slope of ln(k/kref) vs 1/T=−Ea/R. R=8.314462618 J/(mol K). Reference parameterisation reduces arbitrary prefactor scales.
practical: Independently supplied kinetics data
design_task: Determine T for a target k, then check calibration interval and sensitivity. Extension: fit independent rate measurements and examine lever arm in 1/T.
learning_outcome: Move two temperature probes on both k against T and ln(k/kref) against inverse T. Observe why a universal doubling per 10 °C is misleading.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Binary vapour–liquid equilibrium
subject: Thermodynamics
related_theory: Ideal binary at one fixed illustrative temperature, PsatA=2×10⁵ Pa, PsatB=10⁵ Pa; Pbubble=xA PA*+(1−xA) PB*; yA=xAPA*/Pbubble. Pdew=1/[yA/PA*+(1−yA)/PB*]. α=PA*/PB*. An x–y curve with constant α is a surrogate for a distillation exercise.
practical: Published equilibrium data after rights/mixture review
design_task: Recover liquid composition from specified vapour; optional given overall z and P derive phase fractions only inside the two-phase envelope. At pure endpoints both curves meet.
learning_outcome: Drag a liquid composition and predict the equilibrium vapour. Distinguish composition at a given state from the amount of each phase.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: McCabe–Thiele design and reflux
subject: Separations
related_theory: y*=αx/[1+(α−1)x]; xeq(y)=y/[α−(α−1)y]. Rectifying y=Rx/(R+1)+xD/(R+1); saturated-liquid q-line x=zF. Stripping line through (zF,yrect(zF)) and (xB,xB). Start (xD,xD), go horizontally to equilibrium then vertically to active line using x≥zF as rectifying. Stop after horizontal step reaches x≤xB.
practical: Graphical design tutorial; no physical column claimed
design_task: Compare reflux vs stages at same purity and feed. No energy/cost ranking until latent heat/feed rate/utility prices supplied. Stage efficiency and flooding require additional models/data.
learning_outcome: Step stages graphically, then move reflux toward pinch and explain why an apparently small change can make a finite design impossible.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Cake filtration performance and filter area
subject: Separations
related_theory: t=μRm V/(AΔp)+μαc V²/(2A²Δp); c is dry cake mass per filtrate volume. Write t=bv+av², v=V/A; stable v=2t/[b+√(b²+4at)], b=μRm/Δp, a=μαc/(2Δp). Areq=Vtarget/v. Instantaneous flux=Δp/[μ(Rm+αcv)].
practical: Proposed dead-end filtration extension
design_task: For a target volume by a deadline find minimum continuous area, round to candidate elements and forward check. Zero time and positive V is infeasible. Compare clean medium-only limit.
learning_outcome: Compare early medium resistance with late cake resistance. Replicate the same filtration duty across two different surface areas.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: PID control, saturation and recovery
subject: Control
related_theory: Synthetic plant τdy/dt=−y+Kpu+d. Each sample e=r−y; D=−Kc Td (y−yprev)/Ts filtered with β=Tf/(Tf+Ts), Df=βDfprev+(1−β)D; uraw=Kc e+I+Df; u=clip(uraw,0,1). I_next=I+Ts[Kc e/Ti+(u−uraw)/Tt] when back-calculation enabled. Plant exact ZOH update y_next=Kpu+d+(y−Kpu−d)exp(−Ts/τ). τ=10 s, Kp=1, Tf=.5 s, Tt=2 s, Ts=.1 s. Normalised variables.
practical: EXP04 PID flow control
design_task: Tune for settling time, overshoot and time saturated on fixed scenarios, compare achievable and unreachable demands; multiple tunings meet requirements. EXP04 uses measured flow and actual controller settings.
learning_outcome: Apply an unreachable setpoint and release it. Observe commanded output, delivered output and integral state separately.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity, pre/post-lab

title: Numerical integration and timestep convergence
subject: Mathematics
related_theory: dy/dt=−λy, y(0)=1, exact exp(−λt); z=−λΔt; amplification Euler 1+z, backward Euler 1/(1−z), RK4 1+z+z²/2+z³/6+z⁴/24. Apply recurrence; shorten last step precisely to final T. Error against analytic value at same T.
practical: Virtual solver comparison, reuse on CSTR traces
design_task: Choose largest step meeting prescribed endpoint error and positivity; compare evaluations per step across solvers. Use aligned refinements, avoid round-off dominated apparent order.
learning_outcome: Hold a physical model fixed while changing only numerical timestep. Explain how a computed concentration can oscillate in a nonoscillating process.
delivery: Lecture demo, tutorial, guided or independent web activity

title: Fitting an empirical correlation
subject: Mathematics
related_theory: Teaching line y=a+bx+ε; use QR least squares on [1,x]. s²=SSE/(n−2); leverage h*=1/n+(x*−x̄)²/Sxx; 95% mean CI: ŷ±t(.975,n−2)s√h*; prediction interval uses √(1+h*). Extension quadratic fit via QR on centred/scaled x and independent hold-out residuals.
